cases.exposure_context_quote: A 53-year-old male, who was previously in good health, experienced dizziness, nausea and fatigue after fumigating the soil with chloropicrin while growing ginger.
cases.agent_quote: experienced dizziness, nausea and fatigue after fumigating the soil with chloropicrin while growing ginger
cases.circumstance: occupational soil fumigation while growing ginger; developed dizziness, nausea, fatigue, then dyspnoea at 2 days and consciousness disorder at 3 days

symptoms.quote: At admission, the patient was hemodynamically stable but exhibited extreme agitation and delirium (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale, RASS score 3–4), rendering standard Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) assessment unfeasible. Neurological
the patient only exhibited mild signs of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), which cannot explain his state of mental disorder

symptoms.finding: initial dizziness, nausea, fatigue; dyspnoea without fever at day 2
symptoms.quote: Two days later, he felt short of breath without fever. Three days later, he gradually developed consciousness disorders, presenting with unclear speech, irritability and shouting.

cases.time_to_care: consciousness disorder developed 3 days after exposure; admitted via local hospital then tertiary ED

labs.name: blood chloropicrin (mass spectrometry)
labs.quote: The concentration of chloropicrin in the blood was detected by mass spectrometry, and the result was negative.

treatment.name: invasive mechanical ventilation with sedation (midazolam, ciprofol)
treatment.quote: invasive mechanical ventilation was initiated. Midazolam was used for sedation during mechanical ventilation, combined with ciprofol for the first 5 days

treatment.name: antioxidants and hyperbaric oxygen therapy
treatment.quote: Supportive treatment and the application of antioxidants and hyperbaric oxygen therapy were given to the patient.

cases.icu_admission: UNVERIFIED (mechanically ventilated; ICU not explicitly named)
cases.outcome: consciousness improved after 3 weeks; discharged home
cases.outcome_quote: After 3 weeks, his consciousness improved, and he was discharged to home.
cases.notes: Extraction done directly from source text PMC13291128.txt by primary agent after filename-rotation incident; quotes copy-pasted verbatim from converted source text. EEG (increased slow waves) supported diagnosis; MRI generally normal. Diagnosis was clinical - blood chloropicrin assay negative (known instability of the compound).
